entities.name: Pinikir
entities.primary_domains: heaven; love; the planet Venus; sovereignty
entities.source: Henkelman, The Other Gods Who Are; Vallat, RlA s.v. 'Pinikir'
entities.note: Great early Elamite astral goddess titled 'mistress of heaven'; appears in the Old Elamite treaty of Naram-Sin and at Tchoga Zanbil, equated with Ishtar/Ninsianna in god lists.

entities.name: Simut
entities.primary_domains: heraldry of the gods; war; the planet Mars
entities.source: Vallat, RlA s.v. 'Šimut'; Henkelman, The Other Gods Who Are
entities.note: Elamite herald-god ('god of Elam'), spouse of Manzat, equated with Mesopotamian Nergal and the planet Mars; widely attested in royal inscriptions and An=Anum.

entities.name: Nahhunte
entities.source: Vallat, RlA s.v. 'Nahhunte'; Potts, The Archaeology of Elam
entities.note: Elamite sun god and guarantor of justice/contracts, counterpart of Mesopotamian Shamash; element in many royal names (e.g. Šutruk-Nahhunte) and attested from Susa.

entities.name: Manzat
entities.source: Vallat, RlA s.v. 'Manzât'; Henkelman, The Other Gods Who Are
entities.note: Rainbow goddess shared between Elam and Mesopotamia; in Elam wife of Simut, worshipped at Susa and Der; attested in Middle Elamite royal inscriptions.

entities.name: Ruhurater
entities.source: Vallat, RlA s.v. 'Ruhurater'; Potts, The Archaeology of Elam
entities.note: Creator god whose cult centre was Huhnur; attested from an Ur III inscription of Amar-Sin and in Middle Elamite texts, regarded as a fashioner of humankind.

entities.name: Hutran
entities.source: Vallat, RlA; Potts, The Archaeology of Elam; König, EKI
entities.note: Son of Napirisha and Kiririsha in the Tchoga Zanbil / Anshanite theology; invoked in Middle Elamite royal inscriptions for protection of the king.

entities.name: Lagamal
entities.primary_domains: the underworld; judgment of the dead
entities.source: Lambert/Vallat, RlA s.v. 'Lagamal'; Henkelman, The Other Gods Who Are
entities.note: Underworld god of Susa (also worshipped at Mesopotamian Dilbat); in Susian funerary texts the 'advocatus diaboli' who, with Ishmekarab, attends Inshushinak's judgment of souls.

entities.name: Ishmekarab
entities.primary_domains: justice; law; judgment of the dead
entities.source: Vallat, RlA s.v. 'Išme-karāb'; Henkelman, The Other Gods Who Are
entities.note: Deity of justice ('he/she has heard the prayer'); in Susian afterlife texts the 'advocatus dei' who, with Lagamal, escorts the soul before the judge Inshushinak; attested at Susa and Tchoga Zanbil.

entities.name: Narundi
entities.source: Vallat, RlA s.v. 'Narundi'; Potts, The Archaeology of Elam
entities.note: Victory goddess worshipped at Susa c. 2250-1800 BCE (statue dedicated by Puzur-Inshushinak); in Mesopotamian An=Anum reckoned sister of the Sebitti, the 'divine seven of Elam'.

entities.name: Napratep
entities.source: König, EKI; Potts, The Archaeology of Elam
entities.note: Group of 'creator/protector gods' invoked in Middle Elamite royal inscriptions, notably those of Untash-Napirisha at Tchoga Zanbil.

entities.name: Siashum
entities.source: Steve, Tchoga Zanbil III; König, EKI
entities.note: Goddess receiving a dedicated chapel/inscription in the sacred precinct of Tchoga Zanbil (Dur-Untash) under Untash-Napirisha.

entities.name: Kilah-shupir
entities.source: Steve, Tchoga Zanbil III; König, EKI
entities.note: God honoured by a dedicatory inscription in the Tchoga Zanbil temple complex of Untash-Napirisha.

entities.name: Upurkubak
entities.source: Steve, Tchoga Zanbil III; Vallat, RlA
entities.note: Goddess with a dedicated chapel at Tchoga Zanbil; named in Middle Elamite inscriptions of Untash-Napirisha.

entities.name: Hishmitik
entities.source: Steve, Tchoga Zanbil III; König, EKI
entities.note: Deity worshipped (frequently paired with Ruhurater) in the Tchoga Zanbil precinct of Untash-Napirisha.

entities.name: Tepti / Temti
entities.source: Vallat, RlA; Potts, The Archaeology of Elam; König, EKI
entities.note: Elamite 'lord' (tepti/temti) used as a divine epithet and theophoric element (e.g. Tepti-ahar, Temti-Agun) in Sukkalmah- and Middle-Elamite royal names and inscriptions.

entities.name: Jabru
entities.category: Sky / high god (Mesopotamian view of Elam)
entities.source: Lambert, RlA s.v. 'Jabru'; An=Anum god list
entities.note: Listed in Mesopotamian god lists (An=Anum, variant Yabru) as the 'Enlil of Elam'; known only from Mesopotamian texts and not yet attested in indigenous Elamite sources.

relationships.rationale: Pinikir shares the 'mistress of heaven'/Venus profile of Inanna-Ishtar and is equated with her in god lists.
Emar/Mesopotamian god lists directly equate Pinikir with Ninsianna, the Venus deity.
Pinikir was an astral deity identified with the planet Venus.
Simut, the Elamite herald/warrior god of Mars, is the recognized counterpart of Mesopotamian Nergal.
In Elam Simut was regarded as the husband of the rainbow goddess Manzat.
Simut, the herald and Mars-god, carried martial associations through his identification with Nergal.
Nahhunte is the Elamite sun god and justice-guarantor, counterpart of Mesopotamian Utu/Shamash.
Nahhunte was the deified sun in Elamite religion.
As sun god, Nahhunte guaranteed law, contracts and justice in Elam.
Manzat the rainbow goddess was the consort of Simut in the Elamite pantheon.
Ruhurater was regarded as a creator/fashioner deity, tutelary god of Huhnur.
Ruhurater and Hishmitik are paired in the Tchoga Zanbil temple dedications.
Hutran is named as son of Napirisha in the Anshanite/Tchoga Zanbil theology.
Hutran is named as son of Kiririsha, consort of Napirisha, in Middle Elamite inscriptions.
Napirisha is the father of Hutran in the divine triad of Anshan.
Kiririsha is the mother of Hutran in the divine triad of Anshan.
Lagamal was an underworld deity associated with judgment of the dead at Susa.
In Susian funerary texts Lagamal is one of the two assistants escorting the soul before the judge Inshushinak.
As an underworld god Lagamal could be associated with Mesopotamian Nergal.
Lagamal and Ishmekarab form the paired afterlife advocates at Susa.
Ishmekarab was a deity of justice and law at Susa.
Ishmekarab is one of the two assistants attending Inshushinak's judgment of souls in Susian afterlife texts.
Ishmekarab (advocatus dei) is paired with Lagamal (advocatus diaboli) in the Susian judgment of the dead.
Narundi was interpreted as a goddess of victory worshipped at Susa.
Narundi shows partial assimilation to Ishtar-type warrior-goddess iconography in Susa and later Mesopotamian apotropaic ritual.
The Napratep were a collective of protective creator gods invoked for the king's welfare.
The Napratep cluster around the high god Napirisha in Middle Elamite cult.
Siashum was among the deities housed in the Tchoga Zanbil precinct dedicated to Napirisha by Untash-Napirisha.
Kilah-shupir received a dedication in the Napirisha-centred sacred complex of Tchoga Zanbil.
Upurkubak had a chapel within the Tchoga Zanbil precinct of Untash-Napirisha.
Hishmitik is regularly paired with Ruhurater in the Tchoga Zanbil dedications.
Tepti/Temti ('lord') functions as a sovereignty title and theophoric element in Elamite royal names.
Jabru appears in Mesopotamian god lists as the 'Enlil of Elam', a high-god equation characterizing Elam's supreme deity.
